Evan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited about the potential fit. For the next step on Dedicated sizing we do a short token/throughput decomposition so our GPU sizing is aligned to your real traffic shape. I attached a tiny CSV template (token_velocity_sample.csv) you can paste numbers into; a quick reply with the rows below filled is totally fine.

High-level ask (tldr): baseline RPS, peak burst RPS and duration, average prompt tokens, average response tokens, % streaming, session stickiness, and any per-route routing constraints.

Please populate whatever you have; if some fields are unknown mark "TBD" and we can cover on the sizing call.

Fields we need:
- Typical daily requests (approx)
- Baseline concurrency / steady-state RPS
- Peak burst RPS and typical burst duration (minutes)
- Avg prompt tokens (median + 90th pct if known)
- Avg response tokens (median + 90th pct)
- % of requests using streaming vs non-streaming
- % of requests that reuse a KV/prefix cache (i.e., same conversation continuation)
- Acceptable p95 latency for your primary route (ms)
- Model(s) you plan to run and whether you will use multiple model variants (quantized vs full fp16)
- Any multi-tenant considerations (isolated workloads, data residency)

Attachments: token_velocity_sample.csv (attached) — I've pre-filled sample rows for a small shopping-chat app to illustrate formatting.

Next steps: once we have these numbers I'll run a quick model-variant footprint and propose a Reserved GPU pool (SKUs + expected vCPU/GPU headroom) and a short-call to walk through tradeoffs.

Olga

Olga — thanks, attached a filled workbook (vctr-sizing.xlsx) and pasted quick answers below. Left a few trailing comments in the sheet for context.

Summary (numbers are approximate but based on production telemetry):
- Typical daily requests: ~220,000 requests/day (user-facing inference calls; separate embedding pipeline not included)
- Baseline steady-state RPS: ~12 req/s (average over the hour)
- Peak burst RPS: up to ~800 req/s during product launches; typical burst lasts 4–10 minutes and happens ~2–4x per day
- Avg prompt tokens: median 140, 90th pct 420
- Avg response tokens: median 280, 90th pct 1200 (we have some long-form generation for reports)
- % streaming: ~35% interactive chat streams (token-by-token) — mostly short dialogs
- % KV/prefix cache reuse: ~65% of chat continuations reuse prior context (same session id)
- Acceptable p95 latency: customer-facing chat route p95 target 600ms (soft), 95th for batch/reporting routes can be higher
- Models planned: starting with an L2-7 style open model (approx 13B family) and experimenting with a heavier 33B variant for long reports; open to quantized (4-bit) for non-critical routes
- Multi-tenant: single account, but we have isolated customer namespaces; not strict node-level isolation required, want predictable tail behavior

Notes:
- We have a small background job (embedding/upsert) which spikes independently — those are batched and run on a separate job queue (not part of the numbers above)
- Cold-starts are a concern for the 33B variant; we would prefer warm standby capacity or very fast model swap if feasible

Attached workbook has a per-route breakdown (chat/short-response/reporting) and a column for 'estimated tokens per request' that you can use in the sizing math. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform, VectorAI

Thanks Evan — this is great detail, very helpful. A few clarifying questions so our footprint calc matches your expected tail behavior:

1) For the 800 req/s peak: is that dominated by chat-style short requests (lower token count) or by report-generation requests (higher token count)?
2) For burst frequency: are bursts correlated (e.g., all regions) or single-region launches? You mentioned product launches — do those hit the same model variant primarily?
3) On KV reuse — is session affinity sticky to the same server or can requests land on any node and rely on a shared Redis/KV? That affects memory allocation for KV caches vs extra GPU memory for kv-cache-on-device.

Also: Karthik — for the 33B footprint, Evan's description on cold-start suggests we should recommend one warm replica per 8 active GPU workers for faster tail. Can you weigh in with a quick rough delta in RAM/GPU utilization if we plan for warm standby?

We'll schedule a 30-minute sizing call after those answers — Olga, do you have availability later today or tomorrow?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Pre-Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook, very helpful. Couple of quick confirmations and next steps:

- Marissa's clarifying q1: if peak is mostly short chat traffic (lower token tails), that reduces GPU-time pressure but increases scheduling contention. If it's long-report generation, we size more GPUs and add queueing buffers. Please indicate relative split if possible in the workbook (column 'peak_split_short_vs_long').
- Marissa's q2: please note regionality in the workbook — if bursts are multi-region we should consider routing/burst soak across regions rather than single-region over-provisioning.
- On KV reuse: Evan confirmed shared KV — great, that means we can recommend a smaller per-GPU kv-cache footprint and rely on Redis; we'll include a small in-memory prefix cache for hot sessions.
- Karthik will prepare a short delta table for 'warm standby' for the 33B variant and a near-term SKU recommendation (NVIDIA-style SKUs + expected concurrent sessions per GPU).

Proposed next steps:
1) Evan to add peak split and regionality to vctr-sizing.xlsx (or mark TBD) — we can take it as-is if you prefer and assume 60/40 split short/long for conservative sizing.
2) Karthik to produce a 1-page Sizing Summary and a proposed Reserved SKU list (we'll include expected latency curves for median and p95).
3) Schedule a 30-minute call to review the proposed fleet and mutual action plan (attached: VCTR-MAP-draft.docx).

Can we do 30 minutes tomorrow Jul 30, 10:00–10:30 PT? If that doesn't work suggest two other slots.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
